A '''cape''' was a long item of [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] that fell loosely over the shoulders from the neckband. In many [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] societies, wearing a cape was a sign of [[Noble/Legends|nobility]] and power.<ref name="DVRL">''[[Star Wars: Darth Vader: A 3-D Reconstruction Log]]''</ref> That was notably the case on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]].<ref name="AOCVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> For that reason, the [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|life-supporting armor]] of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] was equipped with an [[Armorweave/Legends|armorweave]] cape, as a way to announce his special status as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] personal enforcer.<ref name="DVRL" /> Capes could also visually enlarge their wearers' silhouette to produce an intimidating effect.<ref name="AOCVD" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] ran a piece in their "Life Section" titled "Inside Fashion: Capes are ''Still'' Hot!"

[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] typically wore capes as part of their outfit. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] sometimes wore a cape as did some of his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuard]] bodyguards. [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], Grievous's MagnaGuards, and some [[Senate Guard/Legends|Senate Guards]] wore a cape on one shoulder only. Sith-style armor often had capes both as a sign of superiority over inferiors, and a way of concealing themselves.
